text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures traded at lower levels in late dealings but off the day's heaviest losses linked to disappointment about the quick reversal of gains in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.06, down 0.33 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts endured a seesaw session on Wednesday and ended sharply lower, spooked by Bank of England calls for a half-point rate rise sooner rather than later. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-00/32, down 21/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French 10-year bond futures closed lower on consolidation in a market which, failing to find direction in Europe, focused on nervousness in the U.S. market. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.24, down 0.28 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures held at lower levels reflecting the slide in the lira against the mark and weakness in German bunds, but there was uncertainty as investors pondered the market's next move. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.89, down 0.98 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were little changed in light midday trade as players were mostly sidelined ahead of a Treasury sale of $7.0 billion of inflation-indexed 10-year notes. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-01/32, down 01/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.93 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply down, as the market mood was dampened by large-lot sales in the afternoon. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.07, down 0.30 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was broad-ranging during the morning, including only the second deal with a specific clause allowing redenomination into euros. The EIB launched a 1.0 billion guilder-into-euro 10-year bond via ABN AMRO. Turkey, with 500 million marks, and Mexico, with 500 billion lire, both launched expected Eurobonds. Osaka Gas priced a $400 million 10-year 41 b.p. over.
